description:
FILED s456ag (Opus agent AG, round 13), measured while working the census.
NOT a fix request as it stands: the finding is that the fix is BLOCKED by a
worse bug, and the record is here so the next session does not re-derive it.

THE FOUR CENSUS DROPS: t/re/pat.t:934 and t/re/pat_advanced.t:1235/1255/1285,
all reported as "Ternary operator: Found '?' but no matching ':'", all of the
shape

    1 while /b(?{$foo = $_; $bar = pos})c/g;

PPI reads the `/` after `while` as DIVISION (PPI bug Â§11, the `WORD /` family),
so the regex is torn into `< Operator(/) Word(b) Structure::List( Operator(?)
Constructor{â¦} ) Word(c) Operator(/) Word(g) >` and the stray `?` reaches the
ternary arm.

`Pl::Parser2::_repair_word_match` is the repair for exactly this, and it
DECLINES here for a reason worth writing down: its "is there a closing
delimiter" scan stops at the first `PPI::Token::Structure` `;`, and the `;`
inside the mis-lexed `(?{$foo = $_; $bar = pos})` group is one.  The precise
fix is available -- stop only at a `;` at the SAME nesting level as the opening
`/` (compare parents, or ancestor depth), since a `;` inside braces belongs to
an inner block -- and it was written and discarded, because:

REPAIRING IT MAKES THINGS WORSE.  PCL parses `(?{â¦})` and then STRIPS the code
block silently (probed: `use re 'eval'; my $n=0; $_="aab"; $_ =~ m/a(?{$n++})/g`
gives n=0 where perl gives 1).  So the four LOUD drops would become four SILENT
wrongs -- the worst failure mode in this codebase, and the exact class CLAUDE.md
rule 12 and task #757 exist for.

ORDER: #757's announce-level fix for `(?{â¦})` (or real support) comes FIRST;
then this repair's `;`-level narrowing, and the four census rows leave together.
A population scan for OTHER shapes the `;` blind spot costs was not done --
worth ten minutes when #757 lands.
subject: `_repair_word_match`'s close-scan stops at a `;` that is INSIDE the mis-lexed group, so `1 while /b(?{$x=1; $y=2})c/g` keeps dropping -- and repairing it would turn 4 LOUD drops into 4 SILENT wrongs (#757's `(?{â¦})` class)
